§-refs: §A-stage n = Part A revision stage n; §A-driver n = Part A driver n; §B = Part B; §C-<keyword> = the Part C bullet opening with that keyword; Out n = Output Format item n. O1–O6 are the outcomes agreed at the checkpoint.

## Stages

Track A (Stages 1–3) runs before Track B (Stages 4–6). All six are investigation stages, so each exits with a written finding.

The order diverges from the brief's driver order, which puts seasonality first. Reasons:

- **O1 goes first.** Its covariate is sharp, public and cheap. Its first fit also measures runtime on about 40 years of vintages, which sizes every later stage.
- **O3 comes before O2.** The sample-versus-seasonal-factor split defines what the two-month response is measured on.
- **Track B comes after Track A.** Track B consumes Track A's model, and its answer changes nothing in Track A.
- **O6 opens Track B.** Sample size is the CES-internal covariate, and the budget and staffing stages carry it in their collinear set.

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision scale (O1)
      Objective: Find a written answer to O1, on a reproducible vintage panel and release calendar.
      Spec: §A-driver 2, §A-stage 1, §C-estimand, §C-Cast, §C-Implementation, §C-Validation
      Gap closed: R3, R9 (initial), R10 (one-month stage), R17, R19
      Consumes: Nothing. The package is a scaffold.
      Produces: Monthly CES vintage panel (first, second and third prints). Release calendar with collection days per reference month. Revision-scale measurement model. Measured wall-clock time of one full-history fit.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the collection-days effect on one-month revision scale, with its posterior interval and a LOO comparison against a constant-scale baseline. The panel and calendar rebuild from public sources with one command. The full-history fit time is recorded. R19 is resolved.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Late-sample vs seasonal-factor revision (O3)
      Objective: Find a written answer to O3 for the one- and two-month revisions.
      Spec: §A-driver 1, §A-stage 1–2, §C-Seasonality, §C-Structural change
      Gap closed: R4, R10 (two-month stage)
      Consumes: Stage 1 panel, measurement model and fit-time figure. NSA vintages are added here if Stage 1 did not take them.
      Produces: A per-month split of SA revisions into an NSA-sample component and a seasonal-factor component, usable as a response by Stage 3.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the share of one- and two-month revision variance from each component, by period, with intervals.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: First-closing rate and two-month revision scale (O2)
      Objective: Find a written answer to O2.
      Spec: §A-driver 2, §A-stage 2, §C-estimand, §C-Validation
      Gap closed: R5
      Consumes: Stage 1 panel and model. Stage 2 decomposition.
      Produces: A first-closing collection-rate series by reference month. The Track A scale model with all three Track A covariates.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the first-closing-rate effect on two-month revision scale, with its posterior interval and a LOO comparison against the Stage 1 model.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Sample size and attrition (O6)
      Objective: Find a written answer to O6.
      Spec: §A-driver 4, §C-Identification, §C-Prior specification
      Gap closed: R6, R14 (sample)
      Consumes: Stage 3 Track A scale model and the Stage 1 panel.
      Produces: CES sample-size and attrition series with sources cited. The Track B covariate block, opened under shrinkage.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the sample effects on revision scale, and states which are identified and which are prior-dominated.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Appropriations, continuing resolutions, shutdowns (O4)
      Objective: Find a written answer to O4.
      Spec: §A-driver 3, §C-Identification
      Gap closed: R7, R14 (budget)
      Consumes: Stage 4 covariate block and sample series.
      Produces: Hand-built series for real appropriations, CR months and shutdown months, with sources cited.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the budget-variable effects jointly with the sample controls, and labels as descriptive any effect not identified.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Staffing (O5)
      Objective: Find a written answer to O5.
      Spec: §A-driver 5, §C-Identification
      Gap closed: R8, R14 (staffing)
      Consumes: Stage 4 and Stage 5 series and covariate block.
      Produces: Hand-built BLS staffing series with sources cited. A joint estimate across the full Track B block.
      Exit: A committed finding reports the staffing effects jointly with the budget and sample variables, and states which Track B coefficients the data identify.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/ces-revisions-prompt-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over the accumulated system. Give evidence for each verdict: the implementing stage and plan, any Deviation notes, and any deferred_items entries.

R11 (benchmark and wedge-back) and R12 (hierarchy) have no stage. Each exits one of two ways: a new stage, or a deferral with a written reason. R18 is answered in the completion write-up.

Optional: re-run describe-critique-methodology's Describe mode on the finished system and diff the result against the brief.
